discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 231027
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
627 AM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Areas of fog are possible north of US-30 this morning. Some locally
  dense fog may be possible in far NW Ohio and southern 
  Michigan.

- Warm, dry and pleasant weather will continue well into next week 
  with highs around 70 and lows in the 40s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Fog is the main forecast concern again this morning. Light NNE flow 
off Lake Huron supporting widespread dense fog over parts of SE MI 
and continuing to expand SW with time. Models split on exactly how 
far SW this fog gets but there is a decent chance our NE counties 
could get clipped. A few HRRR and RAP runs have also indicated 
additional fog development possible around KFWA and points SE. Low 
forecast confidence precludes any proactive headline decisions for 
now but will continue to monitor satellite/surface obs closely 
through the early morning and issue advisories or SPS's as 
necessary. Otherwise, incredibly high amplitude/short wavelength 
ridge continues to build over the Great Lakes through the weekend 
with strong AVA/subsidence maintaining high pressure across the 
Lower Great Lakes/northeast CONUS. Surface winds slowly veer to a 
more SE and eventually S/SW direction tonight through the weekend. 
That coupled with some increasing high clouds from upstream 
trough/front should limit the fog threat for Sat AM though some 
patchy fog can't be ruled out for our eastern zones. High temps 
likely reach the low 70s again today given sunny skies (outside of 
morning fog/stratus) and deep mixing. Leaned on the warmer and drier 
side of guidance for today which gives afternoon RH values around 35 
percent. This is not low enough for a substantive fire wx concern 
(especially given very light wind) but imagine finer fuels are 
starting to get pretty dry. Similar story over the weekend. Sunday's 
highs will be a little warmer given increasing SW flow/light WAA but 
dewpoints also creep up a bit as well. Strong ridge holds firm over 
the Ohio Valley this weekend as upstream surface front stalls and 
washes out well to our NW. Our next chance of rain doesn't arrive 
until next Thu and even that is highly questionable as numerous 
solutions show this front stalling to our NW as well. Real rainfall 
chances don't arrive until around Halloween but that is far enough 
out that many things could still change. Main story is that warm, 
dry and pleasant fall weather will continue well into next week.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 622 AM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

The amplification of a low level ridge axis across the Great
Lakes and Ohio Valley will maintain the influence of the
anticyclone across northern Indiana through much of the 
weekend. Easterly flow associated with this high pressure is 
allowing stratus/fog to advect westward into far northwest Ohio,
but expectation is that fog at KSBN/KFWA will remain more 
patchy in nature with anything lower than MVFR vsbys likely 
short-lived over the next few hours before patchy fog 
dissipates. Otherwise VFR conditions and light winds to persist 
through this forecast valid period, and persistence of this 
pattern suggests more patchy fog is possible tonight, although 
confidence of impacts at terminals is on the low side.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...Marsili

spc.text:
SPC AC 231245

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0745 AM CDT Fri Oct 23 2026

   Valid 231300Z - 241200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND
   EVENING OVER PARTS OF NEW MEXICO....

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms with hail, damaging gusts and a tornado or two
   are possible across portions of New Mexico, southern Colorado, and
   far west Texas today into tonight.

   ...NM/CO/Far West TX...
   A large upper trough remains over the western states today, with
   strong southwesterly mid-level winds extending across the southern
   Rockies.  A shortwave trough now moving across northern NM/southern
   CO will depart the area, leaving a few hours of subsidence before a
   combination of daytime heating and subtle forcing within the upper
   jet aid in afternoon thunderstorm development over NM.  Favorable
   deep-layer shear profiles and MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg will support
   a risk of supercell structures through the afternoon and evening
   from southern NM/far west TX into southeast CO.  Relatively steep
   mid level lapse rates and cool temperatures aloft suggest that large
   hail is the main concern from these storms, but locally damaging
   winds could also occur where daytime heating is maximized. A tornado
   or two could occur in terrain-favored areas.

   ..Hart/Dean.. 10/23/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1630Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 230533

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1233 AM CDT Fri Oct 23 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTHERN NEW MEXICO AND FAR WESTERN TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe wind/hail and a tornado are possible across portions of
   central New Mexico into Far West Texas on Saturday.

   ...NM into southwest TX vicinity...

   Strong upper ridging across the MS Valley will prevent much
   eastward-advancement of the upper cyclone over AZ. As a result, a
   belt of enhanced mid/upper southwesterly flow will persist from
   eastern AZ into NM. At the surface, lower pressure will be oriented
   across southern AZ and southwest NM while surface high pressure
   builds across the northern/central Plains in the wake of a surface
   cold front. As a result of the increased surface pressure gradient
   across the southern Rockies, southeasterly low-level winds will
   transport/maintain modest boundary layer moisture across
   central/eastern NM and western TX. Modest destabilization, and large
   scale ascent overspreading the region ahead of the upper cyclone,
   will support thunderstorm development by early to mid-afternoon.

   Vertically veering wind profiles, increasing in speed with height,
   will result in supercell wind profiles and elongated hodographs.
   Midlevel lapse rates will remain modest (to around 7 C/km), with
   cool 500 mb temperatures around -10 to -13 C noted in regional
   forecast soundings. This will result in mainly a large hail risk.
   However, given stronger midlevel flow and somewhat fast storm motion
   (40 kt or so), some risk for strong gusts also will be possible
   where stronger heating occurs. While boundary layer moisture will
   remain modest (generally 50s F dewpoints max), some risk for a
   tornado is possible given favorable low-level shear. This risk will
   likely be focused further south across south-central NM into Far
   West TX where instability and surface heating may be maximized.

   ..Leitman.. 10/23/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 230651

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0151 AM CDT Fri Oct 23 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTHERN NEW MEXICO AND FAR WESTERN TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms, posing mainly a risk for
   hail, are possible on Sunday across portions of southern New Mexico
   and Far West Texas.

   ...Synopsis...

   An upper cyclone/trough over UT/AZ will lift northeast across the
   southern/central Rockies on Sunday into early Monday. A belt of
   enhanced southwesterly flow aloft will persist across the southern
   Rockies and adjacent High Plains. Modest southeasterly low-level
   flow will maintain 50s F surface dewpoints across western TX into
   southern/eastern NM to the south of a stalled surface boundary 
   oriented from northeast NM into western KS.

   Convection is likely to be ongoing Sunday morning, lending to some
   uncertainty in northward extent of low severe probabilities. Further
   south across southern/southeast NM into Far West Texas, forecast
   guidance suggests muted daytime heating could occur across the
   modestly moist airmass, resulting in weak destabilization. Supercell
   wind profiles will again be present given vertically veering winds
   and increasing southwesterly flow with height. Cool midlevel
   temperatures and elongated hodographs suggest hail will be the main
   risk with stronger convection.

   ..Leitman.. 10/23/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
